style.N: You are a gripping storyteller. Read fast (about 3.5 words a second) with the same steady, intense energy the whole way through. No whispering, no breaths, no change of tone between lines. Say Arabic names the Arabic way: Musa as Moo-saa, Allah as Allaah.
style.NE: A young man, about 25, no Middle Eastern accent. Loud, raw grief that sounds real, never theatrical. No breaths.
style.P: A firm, blunt man in his 50s, no Middle Eastern accent, speaking for an angry crowd. Real, understated emotion. No breaths.
style.OLD: A very old man, hoarse and weak but clear, no Middle Eastern accent. Slow, each word an effort. No breaths.

lines: Someone wants this old man dead.
Who would kill a man this old?
He carries the body out into the dark.
He doesn't bury it. He doesn't hide it.
He leaves it at another man's door.
Why would a killer do that?
No one saw. No one heard. No trace.
Inside, a man sleeps. No idea what's at his door.
A dead man on his doorstep.
Soon, they're all blaming each other.
And the old man's nephew is screaming for justice.
My uncle! You killed my uncle!
He's pointing at the family who live here.
One murder. Two sides. Swords drawn.
And the killer is somewhere in this crowd.
One wrong move, and blood runs in the street.
Then the wisest among them shout:
Why are you fighting? Why don't you go to the Prophet of Allah?
If anyone can find the killer, it's him.
They carry the body to him.
The old man's nephew rushes forward.
My uncle has been murdered! A terrible thing has happened to me!
No one but you can show me who killed him, O Prophet of Allah.
If the truth stays hidden, that family takes the blame.
Musa calls out to the people:
By Allah, whoever knows anything about this, tell us.
Not the family at whose door he lay.
Somebody here knows exactly what happened.
There's only one way left to find the truth.
A murder. No witnesses. No one talking.
So they ask Musa to ask his Lord.
Now everyone waits for one thing.
The accused family can't look up.
And somewhere in the crowd, the killer waits too.
Not a name. Not a witness. A cow.
Anger spreads from face to face.
We ask you who killed him, and you tell us to slaughter a cow?
Are you making fun of us?
Musa says: I seek refuge in Allah from being one of the ignorant.
This is Allah's answer to the very thing they asked.
And any cow would have done.
And every question will cost them.
They need a cow to catch a killer.
And they won't stop asking questions. They say:
Ask your Lord to make clear to us what it is!
Musa says: He says it is a cow neither old nor young, but in between...
so do what you are commanded.
Ask your Lord to make clear to us what colour it is.
Musa says: He says it is a bright yellow cow...
a colour that delights everyone who sees it.
How many cows like that could there be?
They're being stubborn with Musa, so Allah is strict with them.
And every question buys the killer more time...
while that family stays under suspicion.
Cows all look alike to us.
Ask your Lord to make clear what it is.
And if Allah wills, we will be guided.
Musa says: He says it is a cow never worked to plough the land...
and not one mark of another colour on it.
Now you have brought the truth.
But does a cow like that even exist?
One cow can expose a killer.
Now they have to find it.
Farm after farm. Town after town.
This one has a white patch.
One cow. In the whole land.
And it belongs to a man more devoted to his father than almost anyone.
They ask him to sell it.
By Allah, we won't leave you until we take it from you!
We found the cow with him. We offered a price, and he refuses!
Musa says: Give them your cow.
He says: O Messenger of Allah, I have more right to my own property.
So what makes one cow worth more than ten?
A merchant offers a young man a fortune in pearls.
The key to his money is under his sleeping father's head.
He says: Wait till my father wakes, and I'll pay you eighty thousand.
The merchant says: Wake him, and it's yours for sixty.
His own offer climbs, if he can only wait.
Finally the young man says: By Allah, I won't buy it from you at all.
A fortune gone, so his father can sleep.
And Allah repays him... with a cow.
A bright yellow cow. Not one mark on it.
The one cow a whole town will one day need to solve a murder.
He won't sell. Not for ten cows.
Musa tells the crowd: Satisfy him.
They offer its weight in gold.
until it's ten times its weight in gold.
But what does a cow have to do with a murder?
The killer is about to find out.
By Allah's command, they strike the dead man with a piece of the cow.
Musa asks him: Who killed you?
Before he says it... who do you think killed him? Comment your answer now.
The man who blamed his neighbours...
who threw dust on his head and wept over the body...
who begged a Prophet to find the killer...
He was standing right there the whole time.
Then the old man falls back dead, just as he was.
The old man had no children.
His nephews were waiting for him to die.
And one of them, his heir, couldn't wait.
He killed him for the money.
He never gets a single coin.
And from then on, no killer could inherit.
No witness. No confession. Allah brought the truth out, from the mouth of a dead man.
Just as Allah brought this man back to life, He will bring back all the dead...
in a single moment, whenever He wills.
Allah tells this story in the Qur'an.
cut: Right where they'll find it first thing in the morning.
Then he melts into the dark.
A Prophet of Allah. And a crowd that wants a name.
He would never say anything about Allah that Allah hadn't revealed.
Not old. Not a calf. A cow in her prime.
They could do it right now.
Not one white hair. Not one black. Not one red.
The whole case now comes down to this one cow.
There's a story behind this cow.
He killed his uncle in the night.
Left him at an innocent family's door.
Then asked a Prophet to catch the killer... himself.
